excerpt: Two original works by medical oncologist and composer Dr. William Stephenson premiered at a free community concert in American Fork.
featuredAlt: Performers from the Reflections concert presented by the Timpanogos Chamber Music Series
html:
For immediate release · September 23, 2025

American Fork, Utah, September 23, 2025—Utah Cancer Specialists is pleased to share that Dr. William Stephenson, medical oncologist and composer, will premiere two original works at Reflections, a free community concert presented by the Timpanogos Chamber Music Series on Saturday, September 27, 2025, at 7:00 PM at Mount Timpanogos Village in American Fork.

The evening pairs new music with beloved repertoire in a program that balances reflection, charm, and brilliance.

At the heart of the program is the world premiere of Reflections on a Journey with Cancer (2025), written by Dr. Stephenson about the deep emotional passage of people facing cancer and the many ways individuals cope with such a diagnosis. The piece, whose words were inspired by a moment of clarity during a hike on Mt. Timpanogos, sets Dr. Stephenson’s lyrics to an existing melody by Maurice Ravel (1875–1937), aligning musical language with themes of resilience, growth, and hope.

A second premiere, Trece de Coco, a trio for flute, oboe, and bassoon, will also debut that night. The program further features works by Poulenc, Chaminade, Milhaud, and others, performed by an outstanding ensemble of artists.

Event Details

What: Reflections—Works by William Stephenson, Poulenc, Milhaud, and others
When: Saturday, September 27, 2025, 7:00 PM
Where: Mount Timpanogos Village, American Fork, Utah
Address: 502 South 1040 East
Cost: Free admission; suggested donation $25 to support the Timpanogos Chamber Music Series

Featured Premieres by Dr. William Stephenson

Reflections on a Journey with Cancer (2025)—the finale of the evening; words set to a melody by Maurice Ravel; inspired during a hike on Mt. Timpanogos; explores the emotional landscape of a cancer diagnosis and the strength found along the way.

Trece de Coco—a trio for flute, oboe, and bassoon, highlighting color, interplay, and expressive lyricism.

Performers

Ray Smith (flute) · Christian Tran (oboe) · Jessi Vandagriff (bassoon) · Tausha Wangsgard (soprano) · Shane Warby (baritone) · Sharalyn Heath (piano) · Carmen Hall (piano), Director, Timpanogos Chamber Music Series.

About Dr. William Stephenson

Dr. Stephenson is a medical oncologist with a long-standing passion for composition. What began nearly 30 years ago with a chance bookstore find—Music Theory for Dummies—grew into dedicated study of music theory and composition. He has studied chamber and orchestral composition with Adam Schoenberg, DMA, and choral composition with James Eakin III, DMA, winner of the 2022 American Prize in Composition, and he currently studies with Esther Megargel, MM. His work for this concert reflects years of disciplined study and a heartfelt commitment to giving musical voice to the patient journey.

Presented by Timpanogos Chamber Music Series

Now in its fourth season with more than 50 concerts presented, the Timpanogos Chamber Music Series brings high-caliber performances to Utah County under the direction of Dr. Carmen Hall, DMA. The Series is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization (EIN: 88-1099934); donations are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law.
